question: Apply the second derivative test to find and classify the local extrema of $f(x)=x^3-12x+1$. Calculate the corresponding extreme values.
explanation:
Critical points
$$f'(x)=3x^2-12=3(x-2)(x+2)$$
Therefore, $x=-2$ and $x=2$ are critical points.
Second derivative
$$f''(x)=6x$$
Classification at $x=-2$
$$f''(-2)=-12<0$$
Hence, $x=-2$ is a point of local maximum.
Classification at $x=2$
$$f''(2)=12>0$$
Hence, $x=2$ is a point of local minimum.
Extreme values
$$f(-2)=-8+24+1=17$$
$$f(2)=8-24+1=-15$$
Conclusion
The local maximum value is $17$, and the local minimum value is $-15$.

options.A: Local minimum $17$ at $x=-2$; local maximum $-15$ at $x=2$
options.B: Local maximum $15$ at $x=-2$; local minimum $-17$ at $x=2$
options.C: Local maximum $17$ at $x=-2$; local minimum $-15$ at $x=2$
options.D: Local maximum $-15$ at $x=-2$; local minimum $17$ at $x=2$
